assumption: Release/root authorization is external explicit trusted control state; content hashing authenticates bytes but does not authorize which root may serve
authority_or_basis: Integrity trust model and no-latest law
if_false: An internally valid but unauthorized root could serve as truth
required_resolution: HQ must designate active-root authorization and lifecycle

assumption: Chosen cryptographic hash algorithms retain acceptable collision and preimage resistance
required_resolution: Freeze algorithm profile version and migration law

assumption: The selected storage substrate provides proved atomic promotion and durability semantics
if_false: A crash may expose partial or mixed release truth
required_resolution: Run substrate-specific crash and durability court or reject substrate

assumption: The exact bytes cryptographically verified are the exact bytes interpreted by query/reconstruction code
if_false: Post-verification mutation or reopen could substitute unverified bytes
required_resolution: Consume the same immutable buffer or require full-member verification before backend access

assumption: Any structure used to narrow a negative/absence search is complete for its declared governed domain and root-bound
if_false: False negatives can be emitted from omitted unverified regions
required_resolution: Prove completeness canonically or escalate to exhaustive canonical verification

assumption: Logical member digests and semantic release identity are deterministic under identical governed inputs
authority_or_basis: R4 replay and semantic identity law
if_false: Rebuild cannot establish same empirical release
required_resolution: Independent semantic replay/equivalence court must fail

assumption: Every object labeled cache can be totally deleted without changing correctness
if_false: A cache has become hidden canonical truth
required_resolution: Reclassify unique/completeness material as canonical or reject cache design

assumption: Physical byte identity is deterministic only for profiles explicitly frozen as BYTE_REPRODUCIBLE
authority_or_basis: R4 logical determinism versus encoder-byte incidentalism
if_false: Byte mismatch could be misclassified as semantic replay failure
required_resolution: Freeze physical profile contract and equivalence handling

assumption: Rollback is explicit and operator-governed rather than automatic
if_false: Runtime errors could silently switch empirical authority
required_resolution: Require fresh target verification and atomic explicit promotion

assumption: Retention of a complete non-serving rollback candidate may conflict with the one-copy steady-state law
if_false: Rollback safety could create forbidden duplicate C11 bytes
required_resolution: R06 and HQ must choose bounded retention law or deterministic rebuild instead

assumption: Transient or in-memory analytical engines remain execution-only and do not persist unique authority
authority_or_basis: Authority 44 and R4 accepted execution path
if_false: A hidden second canonical database appears

assumption: The current streaming full release/member audit remains available after hierarchical verification
authority_or_basis: R4 accepted integrity expectations and C14
required_resolution: Make full audit a mandatory acceptance path

assumption: Root selection never relies on directory ordering mutable latest aliases mtimes or similar incidental state
if_false: Wrong but valid root may become authoritative
required_resolution: Use explicit trusted selector and compare-and-swap lifecycle

assumption: Source-local compiler identity configuration and semantic contract are bound into replay/root authority
if_false: Same source bytes could be interpreted under silently different compiler behavior
required_resolution: Bind exact compiler/configuration digests and require new identity/equivalence court when changed

assumption: A completeness index used to prove absence is canonical root-bound material rather than a disposable cache
if_false: A cache miss could be laundered into negative empirical evidence
required_resolution: Include completeness structure under the root or fall back to canonical exhaustive verification

assumption: Cold canonical members remain equally authoritative and available for integrity closure when relevant
if_false: Hot-only reads could silently omit provenance topology or refuting evidence
required_resolution: Keep all canonical tiers under one root and closure planner

assumption: Physical row chunk bitmap and dense-ordinal positions are not semantic identity unless independently source-authorized
authority_or_basis: C21 and R4 execution-only ordinal law
if_false: Layout changes could alter empirical identity or joins
required_resolution: Bind semantic identity through exact refs/reconstruction rather than incidental order
